readme: THE KEY-IMPORT TICKET, AS ONE FILE, SHARED BY THE TWO REPOS THAT EXCHANGE IT.

vaultody-dashboard-backend SERVES this structure (VaultsController.downloadVaultKeyImportTicket, rendered by VaultsClient.getKeyImportTicket); the VAULTODY Vault Recovery Tool READS it (KeyImportService.sealKeyParts). Both suites load THIS file instead of each building a ticket of their own, because that is how the two sides stopped agreeing in the first place: 264 passing tests on one side and 27 on the other, against two different shapes.

THE SAME BYTES ARE COMMITTED AT TWO PATHS, AND BOTH EXIST: vaultody-wallet-recovery-tool at tests/fixtures/key-import-ticket.json, and vaultody-dashboard-backend at src/tests/fixtures/key-import-ticket.json. Each suite loads the path in its own repo, so `md5 <both paths>` is the whole audit. Changing the shape means changing this file in BOTH repos in the same round - and the other side's suite going red is the point, not an accident.

THE SHAPE IS THE PROTO'S, NOT EITHER SERVICE'S. vaultody-vaults-grpc-messages proto/vaults_manager.proto declares KeyImportTicket.key_import_metadata (repeated KeyImportSessionMetadata) and KeyImportSessionMetadata.players (map<uint32, StringValue>), so the served JSON is keyImportMetadata: an ARRAY of sessions, each with players: an OBJECT keyed by the seat index whose value is that node's public key. Not `sessions`, and not an array of {index, publicKey} pairs: the dashboard's JSON is a rendering of the proto, so the proto names it.

Each session's fields are in proto field order: algorithm(1), players(2), oldKeyId(3), keyId(4), threshold(5), oldThreshold(6), sessionId(7). Compare parsed objects, not the raw text - key order is a readability choice, the names and the nesting are the contract.
oldKeyId and oldThreshold are null on a migration because the proto leaves them unset there: a migration has no retired key. externalKeys is [] on a recovery for the same reason in reverse.

NOTHING HERE IS A SECRET. A ticket carries public values only - node public keys, session ids, key ids, thresholds. The P-256 keys below were generated for this file and belong to no deployment; the production node keys are pinned in the tool's own build (src/lib/vaultodyNodePublicKeys.js), which ships empty and refuses to seal until a release engineer fills it in.
This file is NOT regenerated by a script. It is the contract; a regenerated copy would differ from the other repo's byte for byte and quietly end the agreement.
